Set scores

singscore (Foroutan et al. 2018) gives every biopsy one score per gene set. Within a biopsy, it ranks all genes by abundance and averages the ranks of the set’s members. A set whose members sit high in that biopsy scores high. The score depends only on ranks inside one biopsy, so it does not move when other biopsies are added or removed. This step computes scores and describes them; it tests nothing.

Packages

singscore is called with :: where used.

library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
source(here("00_Setup", "Shared_functions", "workbooks.R"))
inputs <- c(
  gene_sets = "01_Processing/04_Gene_Sets/c_data/gene_sets.rds",
  proteins = "01_Processing/03_Blood_Correction/c_data/blood_correction.rds"
)
paths <- vapply(inputs, here, character(1))
stopifnot(file.exists(paths))

Inputs

Ranking needs every protein in every biopsy and cannot carry a covariate, so the input is limpa’s complete matrix with each protein’s blood slope removed from its observed values (blood_correction.rds, from 03_Blood_Correction). Values limpa estimated from the detection curve are unchanged there.

gs <- readRDS(paths[["gene_sets"]])
proteins <- readRDS(paths[["proteins"]])
targets <- proteins$targets
c(sets = length(gs$sets), proteins = nrow(proteins), biopsies = ncol(proteins))
    sets proteins biopsies 
    1422     2059       48

Sets are keyed on gene symbols, so the matrix rows switch from accessions to the representative gene chosen in 04_Gene_Sets.

gene_map <- filter(gs$protein_map, selected)
stopifnot(all(gene_map$uniprot_id %in% rownames(proteins)), !anyDuplicated(gene_map$gene))
gene_matrix <- proteins$E[gene_map$uniprot_id, ]
rownames(gene_matrix) <- gene_map$gene
dim(gene_matrix)
[1] 2058   48
round(gene_matrix[1:3, 1:3], 2)

GATD3B  20.97  21.47  20.96
ESYT2   15.77  15.77  17.01
ILVBL   14.78  16.54  16.27

Scores

rankGenes() ranks genes within each biopsy. multiScore() scores every set in one pass and also returns each set’s dispersion: the spread (median absolute deviation) of its members’ ranks within a biopsy. Low dispersion means the members sit together; high means they scatter. By default singscore centres the score so that 0 means the members’ average rank equals the biopsy’s middle rank.

ranks <- singscore::rankGenes(gene_matrix)
scored <- singscore::multiScore(ranks, upSetColc = gs$sets)
scores <- scored$Scores
stopifnot(
  identical(rownames(scores), names(gs$sets)),
  identical(colnames(scores), targets$sample_id)
)
dim(scores)
[1] 1422   48
round(scores[1:3, 1:4], 3)
                                      S03_T1 S03_T2 S03_T3 S04_T1
Hallmark|HALLMARK_ADIPOGENESIS         0.135  0.149  0.112  0.139
Hallmark|HALLMARK_ALLOGRAFT_REJECTION -0.044 -0.015  0.006 -0.004
Hallmark|HALLMARK_ANDROGEN_RESPONSE   -0.037 -0.004  0.014  0.053

Spread across sets within a biopsy reflects which genes each set holds. Spread across biopsies within a set is what later comparisons use. Both are recorded.

score_summary <- tibble(
  n_sets = nrow(scores), n_samples = ncol(scores),
  min = round(min(scores), 4), max = round(max(scores), 4),
  mean = round(mean(scores), 4),
  mean_sd_across_sets = round(mean(apply(scores, 2, sd)), 4),
  mean_sd_across_samples = round(mean(apply(scores, 1, sd)), 4)
)
score_summary
# A tibble: 1 × 7
  n_sets n_samples    min   max   mean mean_sd_across_sets
   <int>     <int>  <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>               <dbl>
1   1422        48 -0.404 0.418 0.0259              0.0975
# ℹ 1 more variable: mean_sd_across_samples <dbl>
set_spread <- gs$set_catalog |>
  filter(qualifies) |>
  transmute(set_id, collection) |>
  mutate(
    score = rowMeans(scores[set_id, ]),
    dispersion = rowMeans(scored$Dispersions[set_id, ])
  )
collection_spread <- set_spread |>
  summarise(
    n_sets = n(), median_score = round(median(score), 4),
    median_dispersion = round(median(dispersion), 1), .by = collection
  )
collection_spread

  ggplot(aes(score, group_time)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "grey85", colour = NA) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.12, outlier.shape = NA, linewidth = 0.3) +
  labs(x = "singscore", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9)

How much of the score variation is the person

A principal component analysis (PCA) of the score matrix, then a one-way ANOVA of PC1 and PC2 on the person (subject). The subject share is the fraction of each component’s variance that person identity explains. A large share means comparisons of set scores must account for the person.

components <- prcomp(t(scores), scale. = FALSE)
variance <- summary(components)$importance[2, 1:4]
stopifnot(identical(rownames(components$x), targets$sample_id))
subject_share <- vapply(1:2, function(i) {
  terms <- summary(aov(components$x[, i] ~ targets$subject))[[1]]
  terms[1, 2] / sum(terms[, 2])
}, numeric(1))
structure_check <- tibble(
  component = paste0("PC", 1:4),
  variance_explained = round(as.numeric(variance), 3),
  subject_share = c(round(subject_share, 3), NA, NA)
)
structure_check
# A tibble: 4 × 3
  component variance_explained subject_share
  <chr>                  <dbl>         <dbl>
1 PC1                    0.244         0.698
2 PC2                    0.182         0.405
3 PC3                    0.087        NA    
4 PC4                    0.07         NA

Validation

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(scores), identical(dim(scores), c(length(gs$sets), ncol(proteins))),
  all(abs(scores) <= 1), setequal(set_spread$set_id, rownames(scores))
)

Summary

1422 sets were scored in 48 biopsies. Scores range from -0.4 to 0.42. Person identity explains 70% of PC1 and 41% of PC2.

Save

set_scores.rds holds the set-by-biopsy score matrix (scores); later set-level comparisons read it.

out <- here("01_Processing", "05_Set_Scores", "c_data")
dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(list(scores = scores), file.path(out, "set_scores.rds"), compress = "xz")
sheets <- list(
  score_summary = score_summary,
  collection_spread = collection_spread,
  set_spread = set_spread,
  structure_check = structure_check,
  set_scores = as_tibble(scores, rownames = "set_id")
)
holds <- c(
  "Range and spread of the score matrix.",
  "Median score and dispersion per collection.",
  "Mean score and dispersion per set across biopsies.",
  "Variance explained by the first four components, and the subject share of PC1 and PC2.",
  "The set by biopsy score matrix, as saved in singscore.rds."
)
write_workbook(sheets, holds, file.path(out, "set_scores.xlsx"), inputs, paths)
